profile.subject: Ludwig van Beethoven
profile.overview: Ludwig van Beethoven was a composer and pianist from Bonn who made his career in Vienna, where he earned an early reputation as a pianist and improviser. As his hearing deteriorated, he kept composing, writing piano sonatas, string quartets and symphonies that stretched the musical forms he had inherited.

key_moments.title: From Bonn to Vienna
key_moments.text: Beethoven left Bonn to study composition with **Joseph Haydn** in Vienna. He gained an early reputation there for playing and improvising at the piano.
claims: Ludwig van Beethoven moved from Bonn to Vienna in 1792.
Ludwig van Beethoven studied composition with Joseph Haydn in Vienna.
Ludwig van Beethoven gained an early reputation in Vienna as a pianist and improviser.

key_moments.title: A letter kept private
key_moments.text: At **Heiligenstadt** outside Vienna, Beethoven wrote to his brothers about his despair over his worsening hearing. He said that his wish to continue his work had kept him from taking his own life. The letter stayed among his papers and was discovered after his death.
claims: Ludwig van Beethoven wrote the Heiligenstadt Testament to his brothers in 1802 while staying in Heiligenstadt outside Vienna.
Ludwig van Beethoven described his despair over his worsening hearing in the Heiligenstadt Testament.
Ludwig van Beethoven said in the Heiligenstadt Testament that his wish to continue his work had kept him from taking his own life.
The Heiligenstadt Testament was found among Ludwig van Beethoven's papers after his death.

key_moments.title: The Eroica reaches the public
key_moments.text: Vienna's **Theater an der Wien** hosted the first public performance of Beethoven's **Third Symphony**. The work was unusually long for a symphony of its time. Its second movement is a funeral march, and the symphony is known as the Eroica, or heroic symphony.
claims: Ludwig van Beethoven's Third Symphony received its first public performance at the Theater an der Wien in 1805.
Ludwig van Beethoven's Third Symphony was unusually long for a symphony of its time.
Ludwig van Beethoven's Third Symphony is known as the Eroica, meaning heroic.
The second movement of Ludwig van Beethoven's Third Symphony is a funeral march.

key_moments.title: Voices enter the Ninth
key_moments.text: An orchestra premiered Beethoven's **Ninth Symphony** in Vienna. The first three movements were entirely instrumental. Then solo singers and a choir joined the orchestra for the finale, singing words from **Friedrich Schiller's** poem Ode to Joy.
claims: Ludwig van Beethoven's Ninth Symphony premiered in Vienna in 1824.
The first three movements of Ludwig van Beethoven's Ninth Symphony are instrumental.
The finale of Ludwig van Beethoven's Ninth Symphony features vocal soloists and a choir singing words from Friedrich Schiller's Ode to Joy.

deep_facts.text: As Beethoven's hearing declined, visitors could talk to him by writing their remarks in notebooks. Some of these conversation books survive.
claims: Ludwig van Beethoven's visitors wrote their remarks in conversation books because of Ludwig van Beethoven's hearing loss.
Some of Ludwig van Beethoven's conversation books survive.

deep_facts.text: Beethoven wrote 33 piano variations on a single waltz by the publisher Anton Diabelli. The complete set is known as the **Diabelli Variations**.
claims: Anton Diabelli was a music publisher and composed the waltz on which Ludwig van Beethoven based his Diabelli Variations.
Ludwig van Beethoven's Diabelli Variations consist of 33 piano variations on Anton Diabelli's waltz.

issues: key_moments.1.text: The cited scholarly excerpt says Beethoven held suicidal thoughts at bay through renewed commitment to his art. It does not establish the stronger first-person report that his wish to continue his work kept him from taking his life. Cite the letter itself for the stronger paraphrase, or state that he described suicidal thoughts and a resolve to keep composing.

key_moments.3.date and key_moments.3.text: A premiere asserts a first performance and requires corroboration under the firsts rule. Reclassify the relevant findings and cite the full date and Vienna premiere from both the Eastman study and the supplied Ninth Symphony entry, with independent origins established, or describe the documented 1824 performance without the first-performance claim.
